title: Cities Skylines | Franklin Episode 6: Wooder
premise: The presenter builds Good Hill Water Works, based on Philadelphia’s Fairmount, to argue that useful infrastructure initially privileges the prosperous while eventual health/development benefits and environmental costs complicate the verdict.
coverage: Good Hill Water Works grows from a meteor-excavated reservoir into a landscaped public utility. Diagrams and comic inserts explain water supply before the narration turns to unequal access and environmental costs. Historical and technical claims are the presenter's account.

panels.heading: Opening: Franklin
panels.description: Orange FRANKLIN and white A DONOTEAT SERIES over the completed riverside works.
panels.camera: Title overlays changing aerial angles.
panels.action: Completed works displayed; title transitions to black.

sound.text: Title music: Beethoven Symphony No. 5, movement IV, performed by the Davis High School Symphony Orchestra.

panels.heading: Wooder / the working site
panels.description: EPISODE 6 / WOODER banner over a highlighted building at the river.
panels.camera: Oblique and overhead gameplay views change angle and distance.
panels.action: Structures selected, repositioned and pipes drawn in water-service overlay.

panels.heading: Excavation joke: the boring setup
panels.description: Wooded hill with contour lines before the impact.
panels.camera: High oblique view of the hill.
panels.action: The hill remains intact as a bright object approaches.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the meteor-excavation payoff in the next panel: avoiding a boring time-lapse with spectacular destruction.

panels.heading: Excavation joke: catastrophic shortcut
panels.description: A blinding fireball strikes the hill, leaving a smoking circular crater.
panels.camera: Elevated terrain view, then a cut to the water overlay.
panels.action: Meteor impact excavates the hill; smoke/fire surrounds the crater.
panels.visualGag: A meteor replaces the boring digging montage, followed by the casual “That was easy.” Chirper announces that scientists can inspect asteroid Eliane up close.

panels.heading: From game plumbing to basic water
panels.description: City-simulation building and asset-selection UI at the riverside.
panels.camera: Oblique and overhead gameplay views change angle and distance.
panels.action: Waterworks element selected.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the following Minecraft bucket substitution: abstract municipal supply becomes literal first-person fetching.

panels.heading: Minecraft: carrying the bucket
panels.description: Block-world house, tall plants, and first-person blue water bucket.
panels.camera: Hard cut from Cities: Skylines to changing first-person Minecraft views.
panels.action: Player holds water bucket, then looks into the stone interior.
panels.visualGag: Comic substitution payoff: a different game demonstrates the bucket method literally; connected to prior flowing-water setup.

panels.heading: Minecraft: dig a well
panels.description: Square dirt hole containing blue water; empty bucket foreground.
panels.camera: First-person view looks from the horizon into the hole, then outward.
panels.action: The player looks into the dug hole, then holds a filled bucket.
panels.visualGag: Continuation of cross-game bucket gag: the municipal lesson is played out as Minecraft water collection.

panels.heading: Artesian well: an intentionally crude diagram
panels.description: GROUND-WATER and CONFINED AQUIFER section; stick person beside a spurting well, sun in sunglasses.
panels.camera: Static drawing gains the well and stick figure.
panels.action: Drawn well and stick person appear.

sound.text: Music: “Minecraft” by C418. It continues from the Minecraft footage.

panels.visualGag: Playful sunglasses sun begins a recurring diagram motif; the educational illustration remains functional.

panels.heading: Head above ground / pollution limits
panels.description: Horizontal WATER LEVEL line above the well; later cut returns to simulation.
panels.camera: The static diagram cuts back to the water-service and terrain editor.
panels.action: Water-level line added; gameplay resumes with terrain brush.
panels.visualGag: Sunglasses-sun motif continues from preceding aquifer panel. The later pollution discussion sets up the smiling poop emoji in the following dedicated panel.

panels.heading: Poop in the river: cheerful emoji payoff
panels.description: Large smiling brown poop emoji overlays the water-service editor, with blue river and pale terrain behind it.
panels.camera: The emoji briefly overlays the changing editor view.
panels.action: The emoji appears over gameplay, then vanishes.
panels.visualGag: People dump poop and garbage in the river gets a cheerful poop-emoji illustration.

panels.heading: Roman water supply: introduce the alternative
panels.description: River and newly built game weir seen from above while the presenter introduces distant clean-water sources.
panels.camera: Oblique gameplay view with terrain tools and changing angles.
panels.action: The builder shapes the terrain and weir.
panels.notes: The next photograph illustrates the Pont du Gard.

panels.heading: Roman aqueducts
panels.description: Multi-tier stone aqueduct photograph overlays river construction.
panels.camera: Static image over changing gameplay.
panels.action: Static aqueduct photo; gameplay weir and landscape edited around it.

panels.heading: Limits of aqueducts
panels.description: White bridge/linear infrastructure being placed by the river and hill.
panels.camera: Oblique and overhead gameplay views change angle and distance.
panels.action: Bridge component selected and moved; terrain and road refined.

panels.heading: Open-channel setup
panels.description: FREE SURFACE arrow and a gently descending blue water channel beneath shades-wearing sun.
panels.camera: Static drawing after OPEN-CHANNEL FLOW title on gameplay.
panels.action: Blue channel and direction arrow added.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the exaggerated pipe maze next: ordinary downhill channel contrasted with twisting confined pipe; sunglasses-sun callback.

panels.heading: Pipe-flow payoff
panels.description: Green pipe loops up, down and around a corkscrew, with blue arrows; later horizontal head line.
panels.camera: The static drawing gains a pipe, arrows, and head line, then cuts to gameplay and an aqueduct photograph.
panels.action: Pipe route and arrows appear; head line added.
panels.visualGag: The wildly convoluted pipe illustrates the corkscrew example beneath the smiling sun; it is an exaggerated lesson, not a realistic plumbing plan.

panels.heading: Why aqueducts need huge bridges
panels.description: Photograph of Segovia's tall multi-tier stone aqueduct arches spans an urban square, overlaid on gameplay.
panels.camera: The aqueduct photograph overlays gameplay before the game view returns.
panels.action: Photograph illustrates the height needed to keep the open channel descending.

panels.heading: Roman pipes and survival
panels.description: Selected masonry buildings line the game waterworks.
panels.camera: Oblique and overhead gameplay views change angle and distance.
panels.action: Buildings selected/repositioned; wall extends toward river.
panels.visualGag: Setup for Ottoman homonym insert in next panel; Roman survival story itself is explanatory rather than a joke.

panels.heading: Istanbul aqueduct: serious setup
panels.description: Real aqueduct arches spanning an urban road.
panels.camera: Static image over changing gameplay.
panels.action: No visible character action in the static insert.
panels.visualGag: Setup image for Ottoman furniture pun: the narrator describes later repairs to Istanbul’s Roman aqueduct.

panels.heading: Ottomans / ottoman
panels.description: Ornate red tufted upholstered footstool over gameplay.
panels.camera: Static image over changing gameplay.
panels.action: No visible character action in the static insert.
panels.visualGag: Repairs by the Ottoman Empire are illustrated with an ottoman. A separate ticker reads Pretty Darn Accurate Most Of The Time, undercutting its own authority.

panels.heading: Restoring Rome's aqueducts
panels.description: Game waterworks buildings and selected objects viewed from above as the narration moves from Ottoman repairs to Renaissance Rome.
panels.camera: Overhead gameplay returns before the pope portrait.
panels.action: Waterworks objects remain under editing.

panels.heading: Papal restoration
panels.description: Large portrait of a pope over the site; later fountain/Pantheon photograph.
panels.camera: Static image over changing gameplay.
panels.action: No visible character action in the static insert.

panels.heading: Toward pipes
panels.description: Gameplay resumes with waterworks structures and steep riverbank.
panels.camera: Oblique and overhead gameplay views change angle and distance.
panels.action: Ground leveled around structures.
panels.visualGag: Setup for Mario insert: aqueduct history reaches improved pipe manufacture.

panels.heading: Mario manufactures the punchline
panels.description: Super Mario Bros. screenshot: Mario next to green pipes and a brick castle.
panels.camera: Static image over changing gameplay.
panels.action: No visible character action in the static insert.
panels.visualGag: Pipe manufacture gets a Super Mario Bros. plumber-and-warp-pipe illustration. A separate ticker reads Psychic K.C. Edgar: Predicts City To Grow.

panels.heading: Franklin outgrows Center Square
panels.description: Historical illustration of a round pump house overlays construction.
panels.camera: Static image over changing gameplay.
panels.action: Static historical illustration; gameplay continues before/after.

panels.heading: Goodhill: a knowingly fictional name
panels.description: Large quoted GOODHILL text over river channels and white bridge.
panels.camera: Oblique and overhead gameplay views change angle and distance.
panels.action: Channels and walls selected and refined.
panels.visualGag: Quotation marks on GOODHILL visually underline the knowingly renamed Fairmount model.

panels.heading: Steam-power setup
panels.description: Waterworks channel with selected blue wall/pipe line.
panels.camera: Oblique and overhead gameplay views change angle and distance.
panels.action: Linear element being placed in channel.
panels.visualGag: Setup for children’s-engine insert: the city chooses new steam pumping technology.

panels.heading: The unproven steam engine
panels.description: The Railway Series / Thomas & Friends illustration of Henry, the sad-faced green engine walled behind brickwork.
panels.camera: Static image over changing gameplay.
panels.action: No visible character action in the static insert.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to steam-pump setup: a Thomas & Friends / The Railway Series image of Henry trapped behind brickwork substitutes for real machinery.

panels.heading: Boilers fail; change the machinery
panels.description: Red paving extends in front of the masonry buildings.
panels.camera: Oblique and overhead gameplay views change angle and distance.
panels.action: Paving/linear landscaping placed as boiler failures are narrated.
panels.visualGag: Continuation of the unproven-steam-engine joke and setup for the TWICE caption: boiler failures are about to receive an emphatic visual count.

panels.heading: Boilers exploded TWICE
panels.description: Bold white TWICE appears over red-paved engine-house grounds, a white bridge and Aspen Alexander Street.
panels.camera: TWICE briefly overlays the oblique gameplay view.
panels.action: The one-word emphasis caption appears and disappears while paving tools remain active.
panels.visualGag: TWICE punctures the optimism about steam technology by emphasizing the repeated boiler explosions. A separate ticker reads Staring At Football-Shaped Bladders Good For Concentration, Researchers Proclaim.

panels.heading: Waterwheel replacement
panels.description: Black-and-white section drawing shows a waterwheel and associated pump mechanism.
panels.camera: Static image over changing gameplay.
panels.action: No visible character action in the static insert.

panels.heading: A utility becomes a pleasure ground
panels.description: Green rectangular beds and trees appear on red-brick waterfront; bridge spans channel.
panels.camera: Oblique and overhead gameplay views change angle and distance.
panels.action: Trees, planting beds, white bridge and paths progressively installed.

panels.heading: Protecting supply / making parkland
panels.description: A filled hilltop reservoir has access paths and an ornamental tower.
panels.camera: Oblique and overhead gameplay views change angle and distance.
panels.action: Access paths and tower placed.

panels.heading: What’s the catch?
panels.description: WHAT’S THE CATCH? in bold white lettering over reservoir and clock tower.
panels.camera: Oblique and overhead gameplay views change angle and distance.
panels.action: Camera reframes gardens while objects continue being placed.
panels.visualGag: Visual rhetorical reversal: the beautiful finished/reservoir setup gets its familiar Franklin catch label; immediate continuation explains unequal access.

panels.heading: Subscriptions and no time for leisure
panels.description: Garden paths form symmetrical beds around an ornamental fountain.
panels.camera: Oblique and overhead gameplay views change angle and distance.
panels.action: Fountain, path and lawn layout are assembled.
panels.visualGag: The gardens take shape while the narrator describes people unable to enjoy them, answering “WHAT’S THE CATCH?” with an ironic contrast.

panels.heading: Development rather than immediate equality
panels.description: Top-down fountain, brick paths, grass beds and white bridge.
panels.camera: Oblique and overhead gameplay views change angle and distance.

panels.heading: The weir's negative effects

panels.camera: Elevated gameplay view reframes the landscaped riverbank.
panels.action: Trees and paths are refined while the weir's environmental tradeoff introduces the next topic.
panels.visualGag: Extended setup for the following water-management and purposes/porpoises sequence: serious environmental-effects discussion precedes the topic label and animal pun.

panels.heading: Water-resource-management setup
panels.description: WATER RESOURCE MANAGEMENT title overlays work on reservoir-side paths.
panels.camera: Oblique and overhead gameplay views change angle and distance.
panels.action: Trees and reservoir-side paths are refined.
panels.visualGag: Setup for purposes/porpoises pun immediately following: ostensibly sober engineering topic title contrasts with animal insert.

panels.heading: Multiple porpoises
panels.description: Photograph of two rounded-headed marine mammals fills center screen over gameplay.
panels.camera: Static image over changing gameplay.
panels.action: No visible character action in the static insert.
panels.visualGag: “Multiple purposes” becomes “multiple porpoises” with two marine mammals. They may be belugas.

panels.heading: Four uses, incompatible levels
panels.description: White list: FLOOD CONTROL / ELECTRICITY GENERATION / IRRIGATION & DRINKING WATER SUPPLY / NAVIGATION.
panels.camera: Oblique and overhead gameplay views change angle and distance.
panels.action: List builds over landscaping; cliffs and paths receive rock/tree details.

panels.heading: Navigation depends on usable docks
panels.description: Selected trees beside a path and rocky landscaped bank in the game.
panels.camera: Oblique overhead gameplay before the tweet appears.
panels.action: Tree-placement tool remains active while changing reservoir levels and docks are discussed.
panels.visualGag: Lead-in to the Donnie-from-Queens target reveal: the navigation explanation precedes the narrator's pivot to political wildfire claims and the Trump screenshot.

panels.heading: Donnie from Queens: identify the target
panels.description: Donald J. Trump tweet about environmental laws, water diversion to Pacific, and California wildfires.
panels.camera: Static image over changing gameplay.
panels.action: No visible character action in the static insert.
panels.visualGag: Satirical target reveal links nickname to the displayed tweet; this is a claim being rebutted, not endorsed.

panels.camera: Oblique and overhead gameplay views change angle and distance.
panels.action: Path geometry and riverbank terrain are adjusted.
panels.visualGag: Setup for Hercules insert and grim prison-labor reversal: opening a reservoir cannot direct its water to remote fires.

panels.heading: Herculean labor
panels.description: Disney Hercules cover with cartoon hero and companions overlays gameplay.
panels.camera: Static image over changing gameplay.
panels.action: No visible character action in the static insert.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to impossible river-routing explanation: literal cartoon Hercules visualizes the metaphor; precedes dark actual-labor contrast.

panels.heading: Conventional labor: official-looking setup
panels.description: Unmarked CA Corrections tweet says inmate firefighters include 58 youth offenders.
panels.camera: Static image over changing gameplay.
panels.action: No visible character action in the static insert.
panels.visualGag: Dark setup/payoff linked to Hercules: heroic-labor joke abruptly becomes a child-prison-labor claim; unmarked tweet sets up the red WTF annotation next.

panels.heading: WTF: annotated payoff
panels.description: Same tweet gains red underline beneath 58 youth offenders, arrow and WTF.
panels.camera: Static image over changing gameplay.
panels.action: A red underline, arrow and WTF are added to the tweet.
panels.visualGag: The official tweet gains an incredulous WTF, red underline, and arrow aimed at 58 youth offenders.

panels.heading: Environmental cost / removal dilemma
panels.description: Rocky riverbank houses, trees, shoreline and current under active detailing.
panels.camera: Oblique and overhead gameplay views change angle and distance.
panels.action: Houses, rocks and trees are placed; riverside terrain changes.

panels.heading: A land of contrasts / the long wait
panels.description: White stone bridge and covered central span over the river.
panels.camera: Oblique and overhead gameplay views change angle and distance.
panels.action: Bridge supports and riverside landscape are refined.

panels.heading: The payoff and channel commercial

panels.action: Rock and building selections continue; wide waterworks view appears.
panels.visualGag: The eighty-year trickle-down punchline accompanies the completed waterworks.

panels.heading: Fundraising racket: setup
panels.description: River and rocky banks with gameplay tools.
panels.camera: Oblique and overhead gameplay views change angle and distance.
panels.action: Gameplay continues while channel funding appeal begins.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the Chapo income screenshot in next panel; anti-capitalist fundraising deliberately uses get-rich language.

panels.action: No visible character action in the static insert.
panels.visualGag: The Chapo Patreon screenshot gives the “left-wing content racket” pitch a conspicuous monthly-income target. The figures are those shown in the video.

panels.heading: Anti-capitalist hedge fund / Fairmount acknowledgment
panels.description: Pump-house and planted waterfront viewed above the channel.
panels.camera: Oblique and overhead gameplay views change angle and distance.
panels.action: Final buildings and rocks selected; site reframed.

panels.action: No visible human character action; built landscape shown.

panels.action: No visible character action; water surface varies.

panels.action: Finished scheme displayed; no building edits or visible character actions.

panels.description: White names under My Patreons on black.
panels.camera: Patron credits scroll upward.
panels.action: Patron names pass through screen; no visible people.

panels.camera: Static logo.
